newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says U.S. budget deal only "half the loaf".
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says U.S. budget deal only "half the loaf".

text.p: Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich on Sunday acclaimed last week's budget legislation as proof that a Republican Congress "makes a difference," but said the job was only half done and promised more tax cuts.

Speaking on "Fox News Sunday," the Georgia Republican said, "We cut taxes, reformed welfare, balanced the budget and saved Medicare, and that -- pretty much in terms of what the Contract with America started in 1994 -- that's an historic achievement ... to work toward goals the American people want."

Addressing criticism from conservatives that the balanced budget deal did not go far enough, Gingrich said Thursday's passage of the bill by Congress was a launching point and said there would be more tax cuts in each of the next three years.
He said any concerns that the Republican-controlled Congress had compromised with the Democrat White House would be remedied by more tax cuts next year.

"We are going to move another tax cut in 1998. My point to conservatives would be take this half loaf, put some jam and jelly on it, enjoy it, now let's bake another half loaf in '98, then let's win the '98 election, let's come back in '99, have another tax cut, come back in 2000, have another tax cut," he said.
"These four tax cuts, all signed by Bill Clinton, will move us toward a country with smaller government, lower taxes, more growth. It seems to be that's what conservatives stand for.
"Let's not sit around and gripe and complain because we only got half a loaf when we really wanted to have the whole loaf."

In an early display of drum beating for next year's mid-term Congress elections, Gingrich said, "Now you have proof that a Republican Congress does make a difference. Every family with children is going to have real proof in January; everyone who saves and invests is going to have real proof, everyone who has a small family farm is going to have real proof.
"As people see in their pocket that they have more real spending power the Republican Congress will have more meaning in their lives."

The tax legislation, still to be signed by Clinton, includes a $500 per-child tax credit, credits for college education and a reduction in the top capital gains tax rate to 20 percent from 28 percent.
It also provides inheritance tax relief by raising the threshold at which the estate tax kicks in to $1 million from the current $600,000 over several years.
